title: Aspiration event
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Fictional scenario specification; never imported, published or shown to learners.
learning_objectives: Recognise acute respiratory compromise during feeding and activate the emergency response while stopping potentially unsafe feed delivery.
Do not use a tube again until its position is confirmed by the approved method.
Know that listening over the stomach is not a safe check.
Distinguish initial airway/oxygenation assessment from clinician-led diagnosis of aspiration, equipment rescue and decisions about restarting feed.

sources.use: NICE CG32 nasogastric tube position confirmation statements
NHS misplaced nasogastric tube patient safety alert
Indexed NHS enduring standards and previously mapped SK-11 safety principles; direct current page retrieval limited.
BTS 2023 aspiration pneumonia clinical statement: distinction from chemical pneumonitis and clinical assessment; indexed excerpts only

required_sources: Full aspiration guideline and local airway-clearance, suction and imaging pathway appraisal (BTS 2023 distinction between pneumonitis and pneumonia now linked)
Unit enteral feeding and tube-position policy
gaps: No published clinical scenario may exist until the review phase: this is a specification only.
The branching content, consequences and scoring are the author's reading of the cited sources and have had no clinical review.
BTS 2023 selected aspiration statement supports distinguishing chemical injury from infection; first-line device-specific airway clearance and rescue techniques still need local guidance.
The approved position check differs by country and product; the scenario names no pH threshold.

Case does not teach suctioning, positive-pressure rescue, intubation, bronchoscopy, antibiotic decisions or a validated diagnostic pathway for aspiration; obtain current locally approved airway response and enteral-feeding incident policy.
permissions: Cited sources are paraphrased only; see the licensing register for each source's reproduction status.
setting: A fictional adult receiving enteral feed through a nasogastric tube on a fictional unit.

steps.info: Shortly after enteral feeding begins, an adult develops a new cough and respiratory distress with falling oxygen saturation. Feeding is still running. Aspiration is possible, but the tube position and the cause of deterioration have not been established.
steps.prompt: What is the immediate priority while the cause of respiratory deterioration is being assessed?

options.text: Stop the feed immediately, stay, assess airway, breathing and oxygenation, and urgently call the emergency team. Follow authorised airway/oxygen support with the tube out of use.
options.feedback: Acute coughing, increased work of breathing and a falling saturation during feeding require prompt airway/respiratory assessment and urgent help while the feed is stopped. Misplaced-tube guidance supports withholding use until reassessment, but it does not by itself establish an aspiration diagnosis or prescribe rescue ventilation, suction or positioning for every patient. A witnessed aspiration can cause chemical lung injury, infection or airway obstruction. Assess and support breathing urgently; report visible airway contamination and involve appropriately trained staff for clearance according to the emergency airway pathway.
options.consequence: Stopping feeding and activating urgent respiratory assessment may limit further exposure and allow timely support.

options.text: Reduce the feed rate, observe respiratory effort and saturation for a period and document whether symptoms improve, continuing delivery while waiting to decide whether urgent assessment is needed.
options.feedback: Continuing the feed after respiratory distress risks more harm.
options.consequence: Continuing a reduced feed rate could worsen exposure or delay urgent assessment.

options.text: Flush the tube to clear the suspected obstruction and resume feeding, then reassess coughing and oxygenation before seeking review of the tube position or new respiratory deterioration.
options.feedback: Introducing fluid into a tube of uncertain position risks harm.
options.consequence: Flushing a suspect tube could introduce additional fluid into an unsafe location.

steps.info: At the next shared checkpoint, feeding has stopped and the team is at the bedside. Saturation has improved from the earlier reading, but respiratory assessment continues and the tube position has not been confirmed. A scheduled medicine is due.
steps.prompt: What conditions must be met before any feed, water, medicine or flush is given through the suspect tube?

options.text: Withhold feed, water, medicines and flushes until position is confirmed by the locally approved method, documented and use authorised. Escalate persisting respiratory distress; arrange authorised alternative medicines if needed.
options.feedback: Prior checks or unchanged external markers do not guarantee current safe tube position. Approved tests and documented interpretation are required; resolution of respiratory symptoms alone is not permission to restart the feed. Do not use a trial flush or the appearance of aspirate alone to resolve uncertainty. If aspiration or pH assessment is inconclusive, seek the approved alternative confirmation pathway. The team must also reassess aspiration risk and ongoing respiratory status before feeding resumes.
options.consequence: Approved position confirmation and reassessment may identify an unsafe tube or ongoing aspiration risk before use resumes.

options.text: Restart the feed using yesterday's documented position check, record the current external tube marking and resume planned medications without obtaining the locally required confirmation of position after the new respiratory event or authorisation to use the tube.
options.feedback: Position is confirmed before each use according to the policy, not carried over from an earlier check.
options.consequence: Relying on yesterday's position check could miss subsequent displacement.

options.text: Inject air and listen over the stomach to determine tube position, document the sound as confirmation and resume feed and medicines without obtaining the locally approved verification or authorisation to use the tube.
options.feedback: NHS England's enduring standards reject auscultation as a position-confirmation method; an unchanged external mark or aspirate appearance alone is also insufficient.
options.consequence: Auscultation alone could falsely reassure staff about unsafe tube position.

steps.info: At the final shared checkpoint, respiratory observations have improved and the tube remains out of use. The safety review is under way. The event timeline, verification method and response to treatment still need to be recorded; aspiration and tube misplacement are not yet established diagnoses.
steps.prompt: Which report provides the information needed for clinical follow-up and safety learning?

options.text: Document feed timing, symptoms, observations, verification, interventions and response. Give structured handover and report suspected aspiration or tube misplacement through the safety pathway.
options.feedback: Precise documentation enables the clinical team to assess the event and determine whether it meets the local incident-reporting criteria. A possible aspiration is not automatically proof the tube was misplaced. Aspiration pneumonitis is not automatically bacterial pneumonia. Antibiotic need depends on clinician assessment for infection and the overall clinical picture; do not assume prophylactic antibiotics are required after every aspiration event. After stabilization, identify swallowing impairment or reduced alertness that may increase aspiration risk, including aspiration without obvious coughing. Arrange specialist swallowing assessment when indicated and coordinate a safe nutrition and oral-care plan. Do not infer that safe tube placement establishes safe oral intake.
options.consequence: A factual timeline and documentation of checks and response may help the team distinguish possible causes and identify prevention measures.

options.text: Record that the patient coughed during feeding and symptoms improved; omit the timing, verification method, interventions and team response from the record and handover.
options.feedback: An incomplete record loses the timing and the checks.
options.consequence: A cough-only entry could omit the timing, tube checks and respiratory changes.

options.text: Omit the event from handover and safety reporting because the patient's condition has improved, leaving the next shift unaware of the respiratory deterioration and uncertainty over tube position.
options.feedback: Events are reported so that they can be learned from.
options.consequence: Failure to report could leave a possible safety event and its contributing factors unexamined.

learning_points: New respiratory distress during feeding requires stopping the feed, immediate patient-first airway and oxygenation assessment and urgent emergency-team escalation.

Withhold all tube use, including flushes, water and medicines, while position is uncertain. Confirm with the approved method and documented interpretation before restarting; never use the whoosh test.
A respiratory event during feeding may have several causes; tube position and aspiration require qualified assessment, not an automatic diagnosis from coughing or a single saturation reading.
Distinguish suspected chemical pneumonitis from infection; do not infer antibiotic need from the aspiration event alone.
Aspiration prevention after the event includes safe oral care, individualized swallowing assessment and a documented plan for nutrition and reassessment.
